one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban summarizes former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo's plunder appeal to the SC -- asking acquittal on two grounds and 'going for the jugular' by arguing that if she is convicted for approving the release of P366 million to PCSO (from which she did not personally benefit), then President Aquino could be equally guilty of plunder for approving DAP fund releases. Brief background: after the SC granted bail to Sen. Juan Ponce Enrile, CJ wrote 'By the SC, not by the UN' (Oct 18) suggesting Arroyo's lawyers could obtain bail on equal-protection grounds. But her new counsel, Estelito P. Mendoza, did not pursue bail or rely on the controversial 8-4 Enrile decision or the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention's critique; instead he filed a certiorari petition seeking reversal of the SBN's demurrer denial and immediate acquittal. Recall that the SBN Special Division of five voted 3-2 to deny Arroyo's demurrer, ruling that the prosecution had proven her guilt beyond reasonable doubt -- meaning she would be at risk of conviction unless she presented countervailing evidence. Mendoza asked the Court en banc to act on the petition with interim measures: expedite, set for oral argument, suspend further SBN proceedings, and annul the SBN's demurrer denial leading to acquittal. The 116-page petition advanced two major arguments. First, the Information charged Arroyo and nine others with willfully amassing, accumulating, or acquiring ill-gotten wealth 'in the aggregate amount of [P366 million], more or less'; but since the Information did not specify how much each of the 10 accused amassed, the presumption -- under the principle that criminal indictments must be interpreted in favor of the accused -- is that each did so equally, i.e., only P36.6 million each, below the P50M plunder threshold. Second, the gravamen of plunder is that the public officer amasses/accumulates/acquires ill-gotten wealth of at least P50M; yet 'not a single exhibit of the 637 exhibits ... nor a single testimony of the 21 witnesses ... was offered by the prosecution to prove that petitioner amassed, accumulated or acquired even a single peso of the alleged ill-gotten wealth.' Neither was a conspiracy proven. The only act attributed to Arroyo is her scribbled 'Ok' on the requests for the release of PCSO funds -- no PCSO money passed through, was held, or was used by her or for her personal benefit. As a general rule, demurrer-denial certiorari petitions are frowned upon and appealed only after proceedings are completed; but allowing an exception, the SC swiftly acted upon receipt -- stopped the SBN trial scheduled for Nov 3 and directed the SBN to comment. To CJ's mind, these swift actions show the Court was convinced of the prima facie cogency of the petition; but to be fair, it should have also called for oral argument -- cases of lesser public importance have been orally argued for the enlightenment of parties and people at large. Can SolGen Hilbay -- by law the SBN's and prosecution's counsel -- match the clarity, certainty, and creativity of Atty. Mendoza? Nothing less is expected from the 'People's Tribune.' The column closes with a civic-recognition coda: Cheers to the Metrobank Foundation 'Journalists of the Year' -- Inquirer's Nancy Carvajal, GMA Network's Howie Severino, and Rappler's Marites Vitug -- selected by an independent board of judges led by Ombudsman Conchita Carpio Morales, with the Probe Foundation (Che-Che Lazaro) as cosponsor and CJ Maria Lourdes P.A. Sereno as guest speaker. MB group chair George S.K. Ty was abroad but ably represented by group vice chair Antonio Abacan Jr., MB president Fabian Dee, MBF president Aniceto Sobrepeña, and MBF senior VP Anjanette Ty-Dy Buncio. As chair of the MBF board of advisers, CJ presided over the ceremonies.
